messages:
customer-jd: Hey team — we're seeing a spike in latency and occasional 503s. All our traffic should hit us-west but traces show requests hitting eu-edge. We set X-Client-Region: us-west in the SDK header. Example curl we used to reproduce:

customer-jd: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'X-Client-Region: us-west\0' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat```

customer-jd: request id: req_20240323_12A4F — 95% of requests fine, but ~2% route to eu and have ~800ms extra latency, and sometimes 503 during fallback.

anna-support: Thanks — can you paste the raw request/headers (or tcpdump) and the exact request id? Does the SDK add any control chars or encoding to that header?

customer-jd: attaching the curl output snippet (no tcpdump available in our prod env):

customer-jd: ```* Connected to api.redwood.ai (34.123.45.67) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/chat HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer sk-***
> X-Client-Region: us-west\0
> User-Agent: curl/7.85.0
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

marco-engineer: can you confirm whether you also send region as a query param or cookie? Router precedence matters (we treat explicit query param > header > cookie by policy). If header is malformed it might be parsed as empty and router triggers fallback.

customer-jd: yes we also set region cookie for legacy support: Cookie: region=us-west. We recently rolled out an SDK that writes the X-Client-Region header; I suspect the SDK is appending a null byte when serializing (string terminator bug).

edge-router-bot: Log snippet for req_20240323_12A4F: ```edge[03]: recv req=req_20240323_12A4F src=203.0.113.12 parsed_region_headers=[""] parsed_query_region=["us-west"] parsed_cookies=["region=us-west"] route_chosen=eu-edge reason="header-empty -> fallback-to-query?" latency_ms=810```

anna-support: Repro plan for us: 1) curl with a literal "\0" in header to mimic your SDK, 2) check edge logs for parsed_region_headers value, 3) verify router decision. Meanwhile can you try sending region only in query param as a short-term workaround?

marco-engineer: I reproduced locally — corp-proxy library (used by some SDKs) sometimes emits a NUL character at end of header value. Our edge header parser treats control chars as terminators and ends up with empty header string when NUL is present. Router then sees the header as absent and (depending on precedence) falls back to cookie or default region which for some customers routes to eu-edge. Proposed fix: sanitize header values at ingress (strip C0 control chars including NUL) and add metric to alert when parsed_region_headers is empty but other sources present.

anna-support: Escalating to eng-runtime (assigning to @marco-engineer) and ops for fast roll. Workaround for customer: include ?region=us-west in requests or remove the header temporarily from the SDK.

marco-engineer: patch created: edge/parser: sanitize-region-header-strip-control-chars (PR #4129). Change log: - strip ASCII control chars from region header values - treat zero-length after-sanitization as absent (log with tag header_sanitized_empty) - add telemetry counter region.header.sanitized_empty. Will run canary and promote if green.

ops-ryan: Received. Scheduling hotfix canary rollout to 2 edges (us-west-1, us-east-1) in 30m, full rollout in 4h if no regressions. ETA posted in incidents channel.

customer-jd: Thanks — we'll flip SDK to send region as query param for the next 24h and monitor. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

anna-support: Thanks everyone — marking as triaged and will update the support ticket with workaround and ETA.

marco-engineer: note for post-mortem: add SDK tests to catch trailing nulls and add a lint rule in our client libraries to strip control chars before sending.
